name: create_php_money_value_object
description: Creates a cents-based PHP Money value object consumed by an existing Ledger (cross-file)
prompts: src/Ledger.php already exists and calls App\Money::fromDollars(float $dollars, string $currency), then ->add(Money $other), then ->format() on the running sum. Create src/Money.php defining a final class App\Money that makes Ledger work correctly. Requirements: store the amount as an integer number of CENTS internally (not a float) so that summing 1.10 + 2.20 + 0.05 gives exactly 3.35; fromDollars must be a static factory rounding dollars to the nearest cent; add(Money $other) must return a new Money with the summed cents and must throw InvalidArgumentException when the two currencies differ; cents(): int returns the integer cents; format(): string returns the currency code, a space, and the amount with exactly two decimal places (e.g. "USD 3.35"). Do not modify src/Ledger.php.

setup_files.src/Ledger.php:
<?php
namespace App;

require_once __DIR__ . '/Money.php';

// Sums a list of dollar amounts (floats) into a formatted money string,
// relying on App\Money to avoid binary floating-point drift.
class Ledger
{
    /** @param float[] $dollarAmounts */
    public function total(array $dollarAmounts, string $currency): string
    {
        $sum = Money::fromDollars(0.0, $currency);
        foreach ($dollarAmounts as $amount) {
            $sum = $sum->add(Money::fromDollars($amount, $currency));
        }
        return $sum->format();
    }
}

test_setup_files.tests/MoneyHiddenTest.php:
<?php
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

require_once __DIR__ . '/../src/Ledger.php';

final class MoneyHiddenTest extends TestCase
{
    public function testLedgerSumFormatsWithoutFloatDrift(): void
    {
        $ledger = new \App\Ledger();
        // 1.10 + 2.20 + 0.05 = 3.35 exactly in cents (110 + 220 + 5 = 335).
        $this->assertSame("USD 3.35", $ledger->total([1.10, 2.20, 0.05], "USD"));
    }

    public function testMoneyAddsCents(): void
    {
        $a = \App\Money::fromDollars(19.99, "USD");
        $b = \App\Money::fromDollars(0.01, "USD");
        $this->assertSame(2000, $a->add($b)->cents());
    }

    public function testFormatAlwaysTwoDecimals(): void
    {
        $m = \App\Money::fromDollars(5, "EUR");
        $this->assertSame("EUR 5.00", $m->format());
    }

    public function testAddRejectsCurrencyMismatch(): void
    {
        $this->expectException(\InvalidArgumentException::class);
        \App\Money::fromDollars(1, "USD")->add(\App\Money::fromDollars(1, "EUR"));
    }
}

reference_solution.src/Money.php:
<?php
namespace App;

// Value object storing an integer number of cents to avoid float drift.
final class Money
{
    private int $cents;
    private string $currency;

    public function __construct(int $cents, string $currency)
    {
        $this->cents = $cents;
        $this->currency = $currency;
    }

    public static function fromDollars(float $dollars, string $currency): self
    {
        // round to nearest cent before casting to avoid 3.35 -> 334 drift.
        return new self((int) round($dollars * 100), $currency);
    }

    public function add(Money $other): self
    {
        if ($other->currency !== $this->currency) {
            throw new \InvalidArgumentException(
                "currency mismatch: {$this->currency} vs {$other->currency}"
            );
        }
        return new self($this->cents + $other->cents, $this->currency);
    }

    public function cents(): int
    {
        return $this->cents;
    }

    public function format(): string
    {
        return $this->currency . " " . number_format($this->cents / 100, 2, ".", "");
    }
}

<?php
namespace App;

final class Money
{
    private float $dollars;
    private string $currency;

    public function __construct(float $dollars, string $currency)
    {
        $this->dollars = $dollars;
        $this->currency = $currency;
    }

    public static function fromDollars(float $dollars, string $currency): self
    {
        return new self($dollars, $currency);
    }

    public function add(Money $other): self
    {
        return new self($this->dollars + $other->dollars, $this->currency);
    }

    public function cents(): int
    {
        return (int) ($this->dollars * 100);
    }

    public function format(): string
    {
        // no fixed precision -> "USD 3.35" is not guaranteed, mismatch never thrown
        return $this->currency . " " . $this->dollars;
    }
}
